key_agent_trends: Enterprise CRM platforms acquire specialized voice AI agents to unify conversation and outcome
Frontier labs optimize long-running agent sessions with server-side conversation threading to cut latency
Safety disclosures highlight proximity to recursive self-improvement thresholds in model development
Chinese multimodal models advance on long-horizon agent benchmarks with large context windows
Financial regulators launch governance frameworks for agentic finance including Know Your Agent standards

stories.headline: Salesforce signs definitive agreement to acquire Cresta for voice AI agents
stories.what_happened: On November 2, 2026, Salesforce announced it signed a definitive agreement to acquire Cresta, a voice-first operating system for customer experience. Cresta's voice agents resolve complex customer calls end-to-end while coaching human representatives in real time for brands including Marriott, Comcast and Alaska Airlines. The deal is expected to close in Salesforce's fiscal Q1 2028, subject to regulatory approvals. The Information reported the price at approximately $2.7 billion.
stories.why_it_matters: Extends Salesforce's Agentforce and Service Cloud into high-stakes voice interactions, combining conversation intelligence with CRM context to drive resolution, retention and revenue at enterprise scale.

stories.headline: Anthropic launches Message Threads beta for Claude to speed long agent sessions
stories.what_happened: On November 2, 2026, Anthropic released Message Threads in public beta on the Claude Messages API. Agents send the full conversation once, then only new messages plus the previous response ID; the server retains the thread in encrypted memory. Anthropic reports median time-to-first-token drops of about 35% on 500k–1M token requests in Claude Code. Threads expire after 5 minutes of inactivity and do not change pricing or token usage.
stories.why_it_matters: Reduces latency friction for long-running coding agents, computer-use agents and multi-turn tool workflows without increasing cost, making persistent agent sessions more practical.

stories.headline: Anthropic S-1/A warns of imminent RSI threshold for AI-accelerated progress
stories.what_happened: In its November 2, 2026 amended S-1/A filing with the SEC, Anthropic stated that internal estimates indicate it may imminently meet its Responsible Scaling Policy definition of “dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI.” The company noted it has already used AI to develop models whose capability leaps were not identified at the time and is considering RSP updates to keep humans in control of frontier development. No current models have crossed the threshold.
stories.why_it_matters: Public disclosure from a leading frontier lab that recursive self-improvement risks are approaching its internal safety thresholds, underscoring the need for stronger oversight as AI assists its own development.

stories.headline: Meituan releases LongCat-2.5, 1.6T multimodal model for long-horizon agents
stories.what_happened: On November 2, 2026, Meituan generally availabled LongCat-2.5, a 1.6-trillion-parameter MoE model (approximately 48B active) with native multimodal understanding and a 1-million-token context window. It targets long-horizon agentic tasks across terminals, browsers, GUIs and coding, with reported strong results on agent benchmarks such as BrowseComp and AutomationBench. It is available via API with OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible endpoints and appears on platforms including Vercel AI Gateway.
stories.why_it_matters: Demonstrates competitive Chinese progress on large-context multimodal agent models that can sustain complex multi-step workflows, expanding options beyond US frontier providers for coding and computer-use agents.

stories.headline: HKMA launches Project SAGE to govern agentic finance in Hong Kong
stories.what_happened: On November 2, 2026, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority launched Project SAGE (Securing Agentic Finance with Governance and Enablement) at Hong Kong FinTech Week. The initiative supports responsible adoption of AI agents in finance across use cases, agent identity (including Know Your Agent practices), interoperability standards and legal frameworks. An Agentic Finance Expert Group with banks, fintechs and academics was established.
stories.why_it_matters: Marks one of the first dedicated regulatory frameworks for agentic AI in financial services, addressing identity, delegated authority, liability and interoperability as agents begin handling payments and treasury tasks.
